task_card.title: TTS in Vision: resolve Qwen3-TTS viability, then wire Chatterbox + Qwen as Flows

next_action.description: Build GATE 2 FLOW A - the Voice Changer Flow. Read docs/playbooks/add-flow/ and run /mpi-add-flow. Shape: record a performance (the MPI-573 mic recorder already exists) -> pick a target voice -> FL_ChatterboxVC -> audio gallery card. requiredModels: [], requiredDeps: ['chatterbox-vc-s3gen', 'chatterbox-vc-conds', 'ComfyUI_Fill-ChatterBox', 'ComfyUI-MpiNodes'] - 1.0GB, NOT the 4.25GB TTS set. mediaType 'audio' with the graph's SaveAudio node titled Output_Audio; this would be the FIRST audio-only Flow, so verify the gallery card, save path and group type actually work. Do NOT build TTS in this pass - Flow B is separate and needs performance clips that do not exist yet.

key_decisions: VOICE CHANGER IS ITS OWN FLOW AND SHIPS FIRST (Fabio, this session). It needs 1.0GB not 4.25GB, no TTS model, no performance clips and no voice library - because the user's own recording IS the performance clip, which is the exact asset Flow B is still waiting on. Do not fold it back into TTS.

TURBO IS NOT SHIPPED - for REDUNDANCY, not weakness, and the distinction matters. VC passes laughs/coughs/shushes through natively, so Turbo's nine paralinguistic tags win nothing. It was ALSO never measured fairly: the node hides `exaggeration` AND `cfg_weight` and runs both at 0.0, and cfg_weight is this card's central finding. Do not repeat 'Turbo is unstable' as if it were proven.

ACCENT IS A RUNTIME PARAMETER - FL_ChatterboxMultilingualTTS's `language` selector imposes one on any reference. So the library needs NO accent axis and a user's own voice inherits accents free. This does NOT reopen Qwen VoiceDesign accent, which stays a closed negative after 22 generations - do not merge the two.
Accent routing selects the MODEL, not a parameter (Fabio): none -> FL_ChatterboxTTS (fast default), <lang> -> multilingual (slower). Both feed the same VC stage 2.

Chatterbox is a FLOW WITH requiredDeps - not a ModelDef (forces dead fields + a model-picker entry) and not a Plugin (by its own definition 'not a tile in the Flow Library'). head-swap is the precedent.
constraints: THE WEIGHTS MUST STAY `targetPath`. get_chatterbox_models_dir() computes <ComfyUI>/models/chatterbox/ from __file__ and never touches folder_paths, then hf_hub_downloads anything missing. Move them to mpi_models/ and the pack silently pulls 4.25GB outside the download manager - no progress UI, no sha, no GC, repeated every engine reinstall. Same class as RIFE (MPI-222).

PERTH FAILS SILENTLY. resemble-perth is commented out of the pack's requirements.txt and tts.py/vc.py/mtl_tts.py each wrap `import perth` in try/except, print one warning and ship UNMARKED audio for ever. It is pinned in python_deps.in for EU AI Act Art. 50 (in force since 2026-08-02, Vision is the provider). Gate 2 must prove the marking is APPLIED, not merely installed.

GC HAZARD: flowRequiredDepIds() is what protects a flow's deps from the uninstall guards. The seven chatterbox-* deps are currently owned by NOBODY - safe only because nothing installs them yet. Land the FlowDef before anything installs them, or repeat what MPI-310 did to 5.24GB.

PERFORMANCE AND IDENTITY TRADE AGAINST EACH OTHER - measured from both ends. VC-source exaggeration 1.2 holds identity 0.79-0.87, 1.5 -> 0.70, 2.0 -> 0.61; and by ear, a flatter input picks up the target voice better while a strong performance bleeds the source through. No setting maximises both; every Flow A UI decision picks a point on that curve.

FLOW A USER GUIDANCE, 4 evidence-backed rules: (1) perform but do not push; (2) pick a target that sounds nothing like you - similar voices make the conversion nearly inaudible, the likely shape of an 'it did nothing' report; (3) meet the target's pitch - confirmed this session; (4) hold that pitch steady - drift within a take drifts the output. Rules 2 and 3 only LOOK contradictory: distance in TIMBRE is what makes it audible, distance in PITCH is what you compensate for.

The dialog node is BROKEN for an unrelated reason: torchaudio 2.11 routes .save() through torchcodec, which is not installed, so chatterbox_dialog_node.py:63 dies before parsing a single SPEAKER line. Our own dialogue splitter would hit this identically if it calls torchaudio.save - use soundfile or add torchcodec.

The engine's curated lock covers the shipped path, proven by ast-parsing the pack's imports. The 5 uncovered modules (pykakasi, dicta_onnx, russian_text_stresser, spacy_pkuseg, pyloudnorm) are all lazy; pyloudnorm's try/except in tts_turbo.py is LOAD-BEARING because that file is eagerly imported.

MPI-567 is also live on js/data/flowsRegistry.js, js/data/commandRegistry.js, js/core/operationRegistry.js, operation_registry.json and universal_workflows.js - the exact 4-file op registration Flow A needs. Its claims were stale at handoff time but the card is in `doing`. Re-read state/index.json and expect to coordinate.

Nothing has been installed or run on ANY engine. Ports 3000, 8188 and 48188 were all live (the user's app, the bench, the app engine) and were deliberately left alone. Use CUBRIC_ENGINE_ROOT + npm run app:isolated for the live proof.

DOC DRIFT to fix at Gate 2: docs/playbooks/add-flow/README.md section 0.3 says mediaType is 'image'|'video'; flowsRegistry.js's own JSDoc already documents 'audio' with the Output_Audio law. The registry is right.
